function: Learns RIS phase shifts and BS beamforming (via power features and optimal structure) for sum-rate maximization from uplink CSI, with learned uplink-to-downlink CSI mapping (pp. 5-6).
system: Downlink MU-MISO: BS with N=6 antennas, K=3 single-antenna users, passive reflecting RIS with M=32 elements (continuous or 1-2 bit phases); frequency band not stated (pp. 3, 8, 12).
method: Dual-driven learning: four fully connected sub-networks (CSI-Net1, CSI-Net2, Phase-Net, Power-Net) plus parameter-free beamforming recovery; hybrid supervised (BCD labels) and unsupervised (sum-rate loss) training (pp. 5-6).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rayleigh direct channel, Rician (factor 10) RIS links, path loss from [18], [19]; 10^5 training and 10^3 test samples; labels from BCD algorithm (pp. 4, 8).
test_conditions: Train and test on the same simulated distribution (10^5 train, 10^3 test samples); sweeps of power, BS antennas, users and RIS elements; no unseen-configuration test stated (pp. 8-10).
baselines: Non-learned: BCD with perfect CSI (upper bound), LS estimation with BCD, successive refinement. Learned: GNN [29]; ZF- and MRT-based variants of the proposed networks (pp. 8-12).
metrics: Sum rate (bps/Hz) and minimum user rate versus power, antennas, users and RIS elements; execution time for 1000 samples; training loss curves (pp. 8-12).
complexity: Order O(FA+A^2+FB+B^2+FC+C^2+FD+D^2) plus O(N^3+KN^2+KMN) for recovery (p. 6); runtime 1.43 s versus 42.46 s for BCD, 1000 samples, M=32 (pp. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 8: "We use Rayleigh fading to model the direct channel from" users to the BS and Rician fading for the RIS links, a custom simulator with path loss from [18], [19]; no 3GPP model, public dataset or measurements.
q2_support: p. 6: "different number of transmit antennas, and we can observe that" Fig. 4 shows training loss for each antenna number; the sweeps over power, antennas, users and RIS elements never state that a trained model is reused in an unseen configuration.
q3_support: p. 8: "Perfect CSI with BCD: This approach first assumes that the" perfect downlink CSI is known (non-learned); p. 11: "GNN to map the received pilot signals to the beamformer" is the earlier learned method [29]; p. 11: "sum rate of our proposed method is superior to the GNN-based".
q4_support: p. 6: "The total computational complexity of the four neural" networks is approximately O(FA + A^2 + FB + B^2 + FC + C^2 + FD + D^2); p. 9: "the proposed method takes about" 1.43 s for 1000 samples at M = 32.
q5_support: p. 8: "We implement the proposed network using the deep learning" library TensorFlow [49]; the training data are simulated, with no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Area 3 by the main metric (sum rate); the framework also learns the uplink-to-downlink CSI mapping (CSI-Net, area 2 function) but the evaluation is on sum rate. ZF- and MRT-based learned variants only change the beamforming structure of the proposed networks and are not counted as learned baselines; the GNN of [29] is, compared under reciprocity with LS-estimated CSI (Sec. IV-B, pp. 10-11). Frequency band is not stated.
